title: Building an offer that justifies a higher rate for Solar panel cleaning
audience: Owners and crew leads in solar panel cleaning who quote cleaning for homes and small sites, including solo operators who need to protect the warranty position.
learningOutcomes: Write a solar panel cleaning offer with a clear result, the array named, the warranty position, conditions and a fix-first promise
Identify the friction and risk the customer carries, such as warranty loss, chemical damage and falls, and reduce them
Price a solar cleaning offer on your own hours and access, without relying on an out-of-date per-panel figure

instruction.heading: What a solar customer buys
instruction.body: A solar customer buys clean panels, a written note of what was checked, and a warranty position they can rely on. 'I will clean your solar panels' names a task. 'I will clean the array with water only, photograph it before and after, and give you a written note of what I checked and what I did not check, including the warranty position' names the result and the limits.

instruction.heading: Warranty first, then the price
instruction.body: Solar Victoria says cleaning can be included in an installer's service or done by a specialist service, and warns that a warranty may be at risk if the cleaning is not done by the installing company. Check the warranty before you price the job. The one manufacturer's warranty found in this research (Phono Solar, modules delivered from 2019) excludes dirt stains and damage from chemicals not authorised for cleaning, excludes repairs or modifications by anyone other than an approved technician, and requires a claim within 10 weeks of becoming aware of a fault. That is one manufacturer's document, not a rule for other brands. Ask the client for the installer and the warranty document, and write in the offer what you have checked.

instruction.heading: Tiers, and why there is no current per-panel price
instruction.body: A three-tier offer could be: water clean of the array; water clean with a before-and-after photo note; water clean, photo note and a written warranty check with the installer, if the installer agrees. No current per-panel price from a government or trade body was found. The only per-panel figure in this research is a SolarQuotes article first published on 27 September 2016 and last modified on 4 June 2025. It gives about $7.50 per panel for a single-storey home and $10 for a two-storey home, and says shopping around may find cleaners under $5. That figure is from 2016 and is an editorial view, not a current price. Do not use it as a rate, and do not quote it to a client as today's market. Build your price from your own hours (see the solar BP-05 lesson).

instruction.heading: Do not sell an output gain you cannot show
instruction.body: The same article's author estimates that cleaning twice a year would raise average output by about 2 per cent for most Australian households, and a Tucson study it cites found about 1 per cent. Both are older estimates. The article says cleaning is usually not cost-effective for tilted panels in normal rain, but is worthwhile after dust storms or heavy bird droppings. Treat those as questions to test on your own sites, not as claims for the quote.

instruction.heading: Use water, and say so
instruction.body: Solar Victoria says not to use a pressure hose on panels, not to use harsh soap or chemicals, and that water is usually enough. It says professional cleaners should use full safety gear and not stand on or place anything on the panels. Put the method in the offer, so the client knows what will and will not be used.

instruction.heading: Height and falls, with the Victorian rule to be checked
instruction.body: Panel cleaning is roof work. WorkSafe Victoria's August 2026 release says it makes at least three proactive visits a week to solar sites, that 42 solar companies have been prosecuted since 2021 for failing to manage fall risks, and that allowing workers onto a roof without adequate protection is unlawful, even with no incident. Its September 2026 release describes an installer fined $100,000 in total after inspectors saw workers at about 2.6 to 7 metres without adequate fall protection on four Victorian houses in 2024. Solar Victoria says installers that fail to provide and enforce basic fall protection face suspension or cancellation from the program. The Commonwealth code says roof edges need edge protection and that fragile surfaces must be recognised; it is not Victorian law. Check the Victorian rule with WorkSafe Victoria before any roof access, and do not write a fall-protection method into the offer until you have checked it.

instruction.heading: Keep electrical work out of the cleaning offer
instruction.body: Solar Victoria says a system should be serviced at least every two years by a licensed electrician. That is an electrical service, not a cleaning scope. Do not open isolators, work on wiring or present your cleaning as the electrical service. The licence scope for cleaning crews was not researched, so check the rule in Victoria before you offer any work near electrical equipment.

procedure: Ask the client for the installer and the warranty document before the job, and record what you checked.
Write the outcome in one sentence a customer would repeat, naming the array and the limits.
Inspect the array and roof access at the site visit, and record the number of panels, storey, access and any fragile surface.
Build three tiers, each priced from your own hours and access, with no per-panel figure taken from an old article.
Write the water-only method into the offer, and exclude electrical work and any chemical not approved for panels.
Check the Victorian working-at-height rule before quoting any roof access.
Show one all-in total for each tier and state whether GST is included.

workedExamples.situation: A client with a 20-panel single-storey system says a website told them cleaners charge under $5 a panel, and asks for the same price. The client does not know the installer or whether the warranty has been checked.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: How should the owner respond, and what should the quote say?
workedExamples.reasoning: The owner explains that the under-$5 figure comes from an older article and is not a current price, and that the quote is built from the owner's own hours and access. The owner asks for the installer and the warranty document, and states in the offer what was checked. The offer uses the water-only method and excludes electrical work. Because the job is on a roof, the owner checks the Victorian working-at-height rule before quoting the access, and does not write a fall-protection method until that check is done. No price is stated in this lesson, because no current per-panel evidence was found.

equipmentAndPpe: Package sheet with three tiers and the all-in total
Array record with panel count, storey, access and fragile surfaces
Warranty check record with the installer name and the date it was checked
Fall-prevention and access equipment as the Victorian working-at-height method requires; PPE as listed in {{business:safety.required_ppe}}

commonErrors.error: Quoting a per-panel price from an old or vendor article as today's market rate
commonErrors.prevention: Build the price from your own hours and access. Treat any older per-panel figure as a historical note only.

commonErrors.error: Using a pressure hose or harsh chemicals on panels
commonErrors.prevention: Write a water-only method into the offer, and do not use a pressure hose on panels.

commonErrors.error: Cleaning panels without checking the warranty
commonErrors.prevention: Ask for the installer and the warranty document, and record what you checked before the job.

commonErrors.error: Promising an output gain or a warranty outcome you cannot show
commonErrors.prevention: State only what you checked and what you did not check.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Business guidance only. This lesson does not grant any licence. Victoria's working-at-height rule for roof access was not checked. The Commonwealth falls code (2015) is cited here and is not Victorian law. Check the Victorian rule with WorkSafe Victoria before any roof access.

Electrical work: a system should be serviced by a licensed electrician (Solar Victoria). The licence scope for cleaning crews was not researched. Do not carry out or price electrical work under a cleaning offer.
The ACCC says misleading price statements are prohibited, and a statement about output or savings must be supported. The output figures in this research are older estimates.

qualityStandard: Every solar quote names the array, the method, the warranty check and the exclusions, with an all-in total and GST status.
No per-panel price from an older article is used as a current rate.
Every roof access is checked against the Victorian rule before the quote is sent.
documentationEvidence: Package sheet with the three tiers and the date it was set
Array and access record for each site
Warranty check record with the installer, the document and the date checked
summary: A solar customer buys clean panels, a written note of what was checked, and a warranty position.
No current per-panel price was found, so price from your own hours and access.
Water only, no electrical work, and the Victorian working-at-height rule checked before any roof access.

knowledgeChecks.question: Which part of an offer does the solar panel cleaning customer buy?
options: Clean panels, a written note of what was checked, and a warranty position

knowledgeChecks.question: What should a guarantee be?
options: Impossible to claim on in any case
Only for new customers and friends
Something you can deliver and afford

officialReferences.covers: Taken from the SOL-03 research file (tactic 11); the page was not reopened for this variant. Misleading price statements are prohibited, and an all-in price with GST status is the safer presentation. Publisher: ACCC.

sourceReferences: Solar Victoria, 'Maintenance guide', https://www.solar.vic.gov.au/maintenance-guide, updated 17 July 2026. Supports: cleaning by the installer or a specialist; warranty may be at risk if not done by the installer; no pressure hose; water usually enough; licensed electrician servicing every two years; installers face suspension for missing fall protection.

SolarQuotes, 'Solar panel cleaning', https://www.solarquotes.com.au/blog/solar-panel-cleaning/, published 27 September 2016, last modified 4 June 2025. Vendor/editorial; 2016 origin; per-panel figures are not current; output estimates are older.

Phono Solar, 'Limited Warranty for PV-Modules', https://www.solarquotes.com.au/wp-content/uploads/2019/07/phono-solar-warranty-2.pdf, undated (modules delivered from 1 January 2019). One manufacturer only. Supports: exclusions for dirt stains and unauthorised chemicals; repairs by non-approved technicians; 10-week claim notice.

WorkSafe Victoria, news release on falls risks in the solar sector, https://www.worksafe.vic.gov.au/news/2026-08/crackdown-falls-risks-solar-sector, 26 August 2026. Supports: at least three proactive visits a week; 42 companies prosecuted since 2021; unlawful to allow workers onto a roof without adequate protection, even with no incident.

WorkSafe Victoria, news release on a solar company fine, https://www.worksafe.vic.gov.au/news/2026-09/solar-company-fined-100000-repeated-falls-heights-offences, 4 September 2026. Supports: $100,000 total fine; four Victorian houses in 2024; workers at about 2.6 to 7 metres without adequate fall protection. Installation case, used for teaching.

Work Health and Safety (Managing the Risk of Falls at Workplaces) Code of Practice 2015, https://legislation.gov.au/F2016L00425/asmade/2016-03-30/text/original/epub/OEBPS/document_1/document_1.html, registered 2016. Commonwealth code; not Victorian law. Supports: roof edge protection and fragile surfaces.
Note: Victorian working-at-height rules were not checked for this draft. Electrical licence scope for panel cleaning: GAP.
ACCC, 'Setting prices: what's allowed', https://www.accc.gov.au/business/pricing/setting-prices-whats-allowed, last modified 15 July 2026. Supports: misleading price statements are prohibited.
Note: no current government or trade-body per-panel price was found; no installer or warranty-provider referral evidence was found; no solar runoff rule was found.
